summaries.summary: The page titled 'Biologically Active Amines' displays chemical structures and names of four substances: cocaine (from coca leaves), nicotine (from tobacco), mescaline (from peyote cactus), and morphine (from opium poppies). It explains that alkaloids, which are biologically active amines, are mostly synthesized by plants for protection and that many drugs of addiction are classified as alkaloids.
key_facts: Cocaine, nicotine, mescaline, and morphine are four examples of biologically active amines.
These substances are derived from plants: cocaine from coca leaves, nicotine from tobacco, mescaline from peyote cactus, and morphine from opium poppies.
Alkaloids are biologically active amines synthesized by plants to protect themselves from being eaten by insects and animals.
Many drugs of addiction are classified as alkaloids.
visible_text: The alkaloids are an important group of biologically active amines, mostly synthesized by plants to protect them from being eaten by insects and other animals.
Many drugs of addiction are classified as alkaloids.
